title: The broom
description: A bundle of palm ribs tied with cord. Hear how each day begins with it.

lines.text: And this one is the broom. We call it igbale.
It is made from the thin ribs of palm leaves, dried and tied together at one end.
ask: What is the broom made of?

lines.text: Brooms like this were tied long before anyone now living can remember, from the same palms that give us oil and wine.
ask: How old is this kind of broom?

lines.text: Before a festival, the whole village sweeps its paths and yards, so the elders and the visitors walk on clean ground.
Every morning, before the sun is high, we bend low and sweep the house and the yard.
One rib alone breaks easily. Tied together, they are strong. A family is like that too.
ask: Why are the ribs tied together?

lines.text: When you have looked at it, put it back where you found it.
